scope: Autonomous management of renewable-powered methane plants; research assessment, not a validated controller design.

approaches.name: Rules, state machines and supervisory control
approaches.role: Reference policy and explicit start, stop, hold, trip and restart sequences.
approaches.strength: Fast, legible and suitable for preconditioned recovery actions.
approaches.limit: Rules proliferate as resources and fault combinations interact; local choices can consume tomorrow's reserves.
approaches.evidence: Established control architecture; plant-specific sequences still need engineering.

approaches.name: Mixed-integer economic MPC
approaches.role: Schedule discrete modes, minimum runs, gas buffers, battery and reactor heat together.
approaches.strength: Makes resource trade-offs and forecast-dependent commitments explicit.
approaches.limit: Model mismatch, finite-horizon effects and solver deadlines; an incumbent is not necessarily optimal.
approaches.evidence: Established research framework; specific implementations require validation.

approaches.name: Scenario and chance-constrained MPC
approaches.role: Choose actions against several plausible weather and equipment trajectories.
approaches.strength: Represents recourse and asymmetric shortage costs.
approaches.limit: Scenario quality, temporal correlation and nonanticipativity matter; nominal probability bounds are conditional on assumptions.
approaches.evidence: Substantial control literature; adjacent renewable-fuels simulation studies.

approaches.name: Robust MPC, viability and predictive safety filters
approaches.role: Keep a feasible protective or shutdown trajectory available while accepting useful planner actions.
approaches.strength: Separates performance proposals from constraint enforcement.
approaches.limit: A guarantee depends on valid uncertainty bounds, a suitable backup set and timely computation; excessive robustness sacrifices output.
approaches.evidence: Conditional mathematical results and benchmark demonstrations.

approaches.name: State and health estimation; Kalman filters and MHE
approaches.role: Infer inventories, temperatures, biases and available capacity from noisy observations.
approaches.strength: Carries uncertainty and reconciles several measurements with conservation laws.
approaches.limit: Unobservable faults cannot be recovered by choosing a more sophisticated estimator; model and sensor errors can be confounded.
approaches.evidence: Established estimation methods; MHE tooling available.

approaches.name: Structural diagnosis and residual hypothesis banks
approaches.role: Design independent residuals and determine which faults can be distinguished with available sensors.
approaches.strength: Connects an alarm to violated physical relationships and additional evidence needed.
approaches.limit: Diagnosis is conditional on mode, excitation and the completeness of the fault hypotheses.
approaches.evidence: Mature model-based diagnosis literature and open tooling.

approaches.name: Learned anomaly detection and soft sensors
approaches.role: Detect unfamiliar patterns or estimate unavailable measurements from operating history.
approaches.strength: Can capture nonlinear signatures omitted by reduced physics.
approaches.limit: Novel operating regimes can look faulty; anomaly scores do not identify causes or establish safe recovery.
approaches.evidence: Active process-industry research and commercial condition monitoring.

approaches.name: Dual control and active fault diagnosis
approaches.role: Choose a small perturbation or inspection that improves decisions by revealing health or sensor reliability.
approaches.strength: Makes the cost of uncertainty and the benefit of information explicit.
approaches.limit: Probes consume energy, time and equipment life and may be unsafe or uninformative in the current mode.
approaches.evidence: Research literature; bounded probes are a tractable implementation subset.

approaches.name: Health-aware control and partially observed maintenance planning
approaches.role: Jointly plan production, inspection, service and replacement using health uncertainty.
approaches.strength: Connects present stress with future availability and intervention costs.
approaches.limit: Requires equipment-specific degradation and service data; an accounting wear charge is not a remaining-life model.
approaches.evidence: Operations-research theory, experimental degradation studies and commercial monitoring.

approaches.name: Learning-enhanced MPC
approaches.role: Learn forecast corrections, residual dynamics or a terminal continuation value around a constrained planner.
approaches.strength: Improves a bounded part of the controller while retaining interpretable resource constraints.
approaches.limit: Learned uncertainty and terminal values can be wrong out of distribution; revalidation remains necessary.
approaches.evidence: Broad learning-control literature; 2026 green-ammonia simulation example.

approaches.name: Offline and online reinforcement learning
approaches.role: Learn a sequential policy or value function from simulated or logged transitions.
approaches.strength: Can represent complex long-term behaviour and make fast deployed decisions.
approaches.limit: Exploration, reward errors, dataset coverage and simulator exploitation; offline conservatism is not physical safety.
approaches.evidence: Industrial deployments on bounded tasks; wider process research remains heterogeneous.

approaches.name: Homeostatic and allostatic RL
approaches.role: Represent internal resource needs and learn anticipatory regulation of reserves.
approaches.strength: A useful hypothesis for balancing coupled energy, feedstock, heat and health states over time.
approaches.limit: Fixed setpoints can waste energy; drive reduction can crowd out production; industrial benefit is unestablished by the cited neuroscience studies.
approaches.evidence: Neuroscience theory and simulations, including 2024–2026 developments.

approaches.name: Active inference
approaches.role: Jointly reason about preferred states and information-seeking actions using a generative model.
approaches.strength: Provides a unified language for belief, anticipation and investigation.
approaches.limit: Preferences and model likelihoods are design choices; usefulness must be compared with explicit decision-theoretic baselines.
approaches.evidence: Computational neuroscience simulations; plant application here is a proposal.

approaches.name: Hierarchical and distributed control
approaches.role: Separate slow production scheduling, faster regulation and equipment protection; coordinate local controllers through shared constraints.
approaches.strength: Matches different physical time scales and modular component interfaces.
approaches.limit: Independent agents can fight over the same bus or learn nonstationary environments unless coordination is explicit.
approaches.evidence: Electrolyser control research and commercial multi-plant cooling systems.

approaches.name: Calibrated ensemble and decision-focused forecasting
approaches.role: Estimate distributions of available power and train forecasts against consequences of decision errors.
approaches.strength: Targets the shortages that matter operationally rather than only average forecast accuracy.
approaches.limit: Coverage can fail by regime or lead time; marginal calibration does not establish joint trajectory safety.
approaches.evidence: Weather ensemble practice and statistical/optimization research.

approaches.name: LLM-assisted engineering and operator support
approaches.role: Retrieve grounded explanations, propose structured experiments and summarize recorded decisions.
approaches.strength: Makes complex evidence and controller reasoning accessible.
approaches.limit: Free-form generation does not establish numerical correctness, diagnosis or actuator safety; use typed tools and independent checks.
approaches.evidence: Architectural proposal for this platform, not a claimed plant-control result.
